en: Beguiling illusion has come,
come to the bower-grove of youth.
come to hunt the heart,
come with secret footsteps,
come in gold-ray-tangled darkness.
It laid the noose of sorcery,
in wind upon wind, in shadow upon shadow
it plays the flute.
It tries the valor of the hero,
it strikes at the sage's hallowed vows,
the snare-net of ruin has closed on every side.
Come, beauty unadorned,
come, truth without pride —
strike down the fortress of dream,
bring freedom, bring it,
severing the bonds of deceit
come to the rescue of manhood.
Rumbling, rumbling, rumbling, rumbling — the dense clouds thunder on the mountain peak,
in the forest, shadow of darkness.
In the cascade's babbling tumult
the timid cannot hear the hunter's footfall:
the deer couple.
The leopard — its claw-print rows
it has left upon the mire of that path,
step by step it has given away the lair's whereabouts.
Oh, what unbearable audacity!
Whoever holds Arjuna in scorn —
where will he find his refuge!
Arjuna! You, Arjuna!
Haha, haha, haha, haha — you band of boys,
run along to your mother's lap; there is nothing to fear.
Oh, what a strange jest!
Arjuna! You! Arjuna!
Come back, come back,
do not dishonor me with forgiveness,
summon me to battle!
The glory of death at a hero's hand —
let me feel it —
Arjuna! You, Arjuna!
Ah, luckless woman — what a welcome for the great!
The god of your world came,
and went away,
went — went deceiving you —
Arjuna! You, Arjuna!
The day drifts by,
tell me —
to which forest shall I go hunting.
Under kohl-black clouds, in the moist wind,
the deer go racing in the bamboo grove's shade.
Enough, enough — why this empty game any more.
Life has turned to distaste,
and scorn upon my own self.
O storm, come down — come, oh come, to my
branch of withered leaves,
in this monsoon, at the new Dark One's
hour of arrival.
Whatever is listless, whatever lifeless,
whatever has lost its joy,
in the tear-stream of the final night
let it today be done;
let what must go, go its way
to the beat of the fierce dance.
My seat must be laid
in the room of the emptied heart,
new garments must be worn
upon the drenched breast.
A flood has called in the river's waters,
its banks have floated away,
the fragrant word of the jasmine grove
has rushed away, destination unknown —
my soul has woken, surely,
behind the veil of death.
Beloved, what light has touched my eyes!
Surely you dwelt as radiance in the sun's realm!
My heart remained waiting for you
age after age, through day and night,
it dwelt in darkness thick with heartache,
birth after birth passed in parting's grief.
An unopened bud in the bower-grove,
with a sorrowful mind empty of song —
companionless, this endless sorrow-night —
shall I wear it out, spreading my bed in solitude!
O beautiful one, O beautiful one,
come bearing your bridal garland,
cast away the veil's shadow
and behold the shy smiling face in blessed light.
Go, if you would go — then
you will have to return.
In futile tears
I will not grovel in the dust,
I shall not, shall not go quenching the lamp
at the festival of my life.
My striving is not timid,
my strength shall be freed
though the door remain barred.
I do not fear the averse moment —
Victory will come, victory will come, victory will come,
day by day, the knot of your heart
I shall untie in the glory of love.
Moment upon moment, deep in my mind, I hear
the call of fathomless waters.
The mind stays not, stays not, stays not at home,
restless heart.
I will set myself adrift
on the brimming tide,
in the current that drowns all care
I will bathe.
The burning of futile desire
shall be extinguished.
A wave has stirred the water.
A wave has stirred my heart's floor.
What restlessness today in the sky,
in this wind —
as if a restless apsara's flying scarf
bestows a shiver of thrill,
on a far sea-strand, in whose anklets —
a humming strain.
Make me new, all of you, make me new
in new adornment.
Under late autumn's curse
the garden-ground lies stripped and destitute;
in spring let its poverty be lifted
by new wealth of loveliness.
Let the bare branch forget its shame
in a mantle of leaves.
Let it sound, by love's enchanted spell,
on the vina of the thrilling heart:
homage to the Ever-Beautiful.
Let joy-restless dance stream through limb after limb
in wave upon wave,
let youth receive its honor
in the longed-for union.
I will offer up to you
my heart, my life, my mind!
Forgive me,
I am not worthy of choosing, fair lady —
a celibate, vow-bound.
Alas, alas — I have failed womankind
through the long years of my life.
Shame on bow and arrow!
Shame on the arm's might!
One moment's rushing tear-flood
swept away my discipline of manhood.
With the long sighs of unfulfilled youth
it made the spring distraught.
A spring so full of weeping
has surely never come before.
It has dyed my parting's pain
in the kinshuk's crimson glow.
Forgive me,
I am not worthy of choosing, fair lady —
a celibate, vow-bound.
A spring so full of weeping
has surely never come before.
It has dyed my parting's pain
in the kinshuk's crimson glow.
At the bower's gate the wild jasmine
has dressed herself in fresh new leaves,
all day and night, unblinking,
she wakes watching for whose path.
On the south wind, in the far sky,
a lone parted lover sings, it seems.
In my bower-grove all the buds
long to tear their binding sheaths.
At the barred door of this heart I
strike with desperate hands over and over,
that I could not give myself —
this is the ache that weighs on my mind.
In your Baishakh there was
the burning of fierce sunlight,
when did the rain-clouds
bring on Ashadh's turn —
Alas, alas, alas.
How it lay hidden in the hard stone —
suddenly a waterfall
came down, pouring tears.
Alas, alas, alas.
To hunt the deer
she who went out to the forest —
turned doe at the last,
has the helpless girl come?
Alas, alas, alas.
She who dwelt in her own
strength's proud assurance —
to whose feet does she bring
the offering-tray of admitted defeat.
Alas, alas, alas.
This empty basket of mine
I will lay at your feet.
I will give a beggar-woman's veil,
spreading it along your every path.
With the blossoms you string your flower-bow,
with those very flowers, O bodiless god,
the poverty of my offered worship
take away.
On your campaign of conquest
take me with you,
the flower-arrow's mark upon my brow —
paint it there!
If you fill my emptiness
with brimming nectar,
I will raise your victory-cry
in proclamation;
Waken the summons of Phalgun
in this body of mine
with the southern breeze.
Manipur's royal daughter,
I know you,
ascetic maiden.
Your mind was not on my worship,
then why, without reason,
did you come to my door, young woman?
Speak, speak, let me hear.
I was schooled in the learning of men;
I never gained initiation in winning hearts —
O flower-bowed god —
this young body is stung with insult.
Arjuna the celibate
saw no woman in my face;
he turned me away, and went back.
Have mercy on this luckless one —
for only a single year
in flower-loveliness
let my body take your heaven's worth,
matchless upon earth.
Therefore I granted the boon:
in your sidelong glance shall dwell the fifth arrow,
my fifth arrow —
it will bewitch the mind,
the woman-defying ascetic
you shall win before long,
you will make him captive in your arms' noose
with a mocking smile.
The princess of Manipur
shall be blessed in her beloved's heart-conquest.
Who plays the flute through every limb of mine?
In joy, in sorrow, my mind drifts far away.
With the tune of flowers unfolding
body and mind rise brimming,
what sweetness, what fragrance
goes floating on the wind.
Suddenly hope wakes in my mind:
my offering has found the language of fire.
Today in my beauty, in my dress,
to whom do I write this letter?
The heart's captive word has come, breaking its bonds.
O fish-bannered god,
what great demoness have you bound
and made her my body's companion?
This illusive loveliness of mine — what a curse!
The fleeting flood of youth,
surging in waves through my blood-stream,
has driven me mad.
This madness mingled with dream-heady intoxication —
what vast pain it wakes in body and mind.
It courses through my every vein —
what a burning, what a torrent —
in a flash a lightning-vine darts through my whole body.
In the storm-wind's roar I lose myself,
in the wild, restless flood that youth has churned.
Waves rise in my heart —
toward whom, upon the horizon?
It weeps in the language of hints —
there are no, no words.
Forgive her, friend,
she came only to beguile your eyes,
only to swing you a brief while on enchantment's swing,
to beguile your eyes.
Down she came from the city of illusion,
she brought with her the key of dreams
to unlock the hard door of your heart,
to beguile your eyes.
Whom have I beheld!
Is she real, is she illusion,
is she flesh,
is she a shadow tinted with golden rays!
Come, come, whoever you may be,
say it, say you are not a dream.
The flawless beauty of her body's vine
bears the fullness of all longing.
You are a guest, my guest.
Tell me by what name I should honor you.
I am the Pandava Arjuna, Gandiva-bearer,
O king's daughter.
Take my fame,
take my renown,
take my manhood's pride.
Take my all.
